refuted_or_hollow.claim: The InfoBunker facility in Boone County, Iowa was 'purpose-built by the military' as a 'former Government Command Bunker'.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: InfoBunker LLC's own marketing copy (infobunker.com and its overview page), reproduced verbatim across data-centre directories (datacentermap, baxtel, datacentercatalog, ocolo, cloudandcolocation), aggregator listicles ('10 Largest Underground Data Centers in the World'), and trade coverage.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Every account independent of the operator attributes construction and ownership to AT&T Long Lines: the CLUI Land Use Database calls it 'a former AT&T equipment bunker' with a surface microwave relay tower 'built as part of AT&T's nationwide communications system in the 1960s'; the Wikimapia annotation calls it a former AT&T AUTOVON facility; and it sits within the Long Lines corpus. The claim is also self-refuting on its own expected records: if the military had built it, a MILCON line, a federal deed and a service real-property entry would all be X3 expectations, and none has been produced by anyone in twenty years of the facility being publicly marketed. Under §2.5 the operator is the claimant and the claim is the product, so the assertion is excluded from V entirely and is evidence for ORIGIN only.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A common carrier built a hardened equipment building to carry, among other traffic, military circuits under contract. 'Built by AT&T for a network that served the military' has been compressed in marketing copy into 'built by the military'. This is an ordinary and probably not even cynical elision, but it is false, and it materially changes what a reader thinks the building is.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: This particular bunker was designed to withstand a 20-megaton nuclear detonation at 2.5 miles — asserted of InfoBunker, of Lyons, and of assorted Long Lines sites generally.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A document transcribed as 'Nuclear Design of AT&T Equipment' at qsl.net/n9zia/Nuclear_Design.htm, which sets out AT&T design ASSUMPTIONS — 2.5 miles from a 20-megaton blast, 1000 mph wind, 40 G shock wave, high-velocity debris, and an 'Extremely Hard Design (50 PSI)' class. From there it entered the Hackaday feature 'Horns Across America: The AT&T Long Lines Network' (2017) and the general Long Lines literature, and thence into individual sites' marketing and into hundreds of pages.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Not because the figure is false — it appears to be a genuine AT&T design criterion — but because it is a PROGRAMME-LEVEL specification for one hardness class being applied to INSTANCES whose class is undocumented. The same corpus states that many L-3I facilities were designed for a maximum of about 2 psi overpressure, which is a completely different structure from a 50 psi 'extremely hard' design. Applying the extreme figure to an arbitrary Long Lines building is the CLASS-scope error §2.4 exists to block, and it is the single most-copied error in this literature. A secondary problem: I could not establish what the qsl.net page is a transcription OF — no Bell System Practice number, no Bell Laboratories Record citation, no accession. The most-quoted number on the beat has no traceable document behind it that I could find.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: AT&T published design criteria for several hardness classes across a network of over a hundred main stations, a thousand repeater vaults and several hundred unhardened repeaters. A single dramatic number from the top of that range has detached from its class and now floats freely. The correct statement for any individual site is: unknown, pending an instance-level engineering record.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The AT&T Project Offices were built to shelter senior federal officials in a nuclear attack — stated as established fact.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Albert LaFrance, coldwar-c4i.net, who states it as inference and hedges it explicitly and repeatedly: AUTOVON switching was 'probably not the station's primary mission', the AUTOVON equipment was installed 'to serve another activity', it is 'likely' the stations supported a classified continuity-of-government programme, and they 'may have served' as a relocation site.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Not hollow as a hypothesis — it is a reasonable and possibly correct one, advanced honestly by a named researcher who marked it as conjecture. It is hollow as a CITATION. Wikipedia's 'Project Offices' article, the CLUI database entries, and every downstream retelling (War History Online, OnlyInYourState, realtor blogs, Free Republic threads, YouTube summaries, and a Grokipedia mirror) restate the conclusion with the hedges removed, and the resulting appearance of many converging sources is one researcher's stated conjecture reflected in many mirrors. Under §5.3 this is the citogenesis pattern precisely: a hedge-stripping laundering loop, which caps the laundered proposition at E and attaches the flag to the proposition rather than to the site. The sites are real; the buildings are real; the AUTOVON role is well supported. The sheltering claim is one inference, and after twenty years no primary record has surfaced for it in the open index.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: DoD required AUTOVON switches to survive nuclear attack and specified them accordingly. Every physical feature offered in support of the sheltering claim — earth cover, blast valves, decontamination bay, standby generation, filtered ventilation, remote siting, elevated security — is fully produced by the switching mission alone. The single observation that does NOT reduce to the switching mission is the Greenbrier switchboard reportedly labelled 'CHATAM' and 'HGRSTOWN', and even that establishes a communications relationship rather than a sheltering role.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The Big Hole facility in Chatham County inspired the laboratory in the television series Stranger Things.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Indy Week culture-section pieces ('Is there more to Big Hole?' / 'Does a Secretive Underground Pittsboro Facility Serve as Inspiration for the Stranger Things Lab?'), subsequently repeated by regional listicle and tourism sites.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: No production-side sourcing was found — no statement by the series' creators, no production document, no interview. The piece is framed as a question in its own headline. The claim's continued circulation as though settled is a pure amplification artefact and it does no evidentiary work of any kind for any proposition about the facility. I record it because it is the most-shared fact about this site and because a register that ingests popularity will ingest it.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A local outlet wrote a speculative culture piece connecting a locally famous mysterious facility to a locally popular television programme. That is the entire event.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: The Netcong / Roxbury underground facility is 125,000 square feet.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Vital Records Incorporated's own facility page for the Roxbury vault.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Not refuted, but inadmissible and in conflict. The independent surveyor (CLUI) states 86,000 square feet — a 45 per cent discrepancy. The larger figure is SELF-PUBLISHED by a party that sells storage by the square foot, which under §2.4 excludes it from V outright and, under §4.4, makes it anti-diagnostic: a commercial incentive to state the larger number fully explains the larger number. The likely reconciliation is that the figures measure different things, but that is inference. The register's correct position is that the only admissible figure is CLUI's, that CLUI does not show its working either, and that the question is open pending a municipal assessment record.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Gross structural area and marketable usable area are different numbers, and vendors quote the flattering one. No deception need be involved for the register to be unable to use it.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Peters Mountain received $61 million of Albemarle County-permitted works in 2007.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: The Wikipedia article 'Project Offices', which attributes the figure to Albemarle County building permits without a permit number, date, or applicant name. Repeated onward by Wikimapia annotation and by the Grokipedia mirror.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Untraced rather than refuted, and flagged here because it is the highest-diagnosticity number I encountered and simultaneously the one most likely to be wrong. It is exactly the profile of a fact that propagates: specific, plausible, attributed to a real and authoritative record class, and unaccompanied by any identifier that would let anyone check it. Albemarle County operates a public building-permit document viewer, so the check is cheap and has apparently never been published. Until it resolves, the honest statement is that a wiki asserts a county record exists; that is a claim about a record, not a record.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Large carrier capital projects at existing network nodes are routine, and $61 million, while extraordinary for a relay hut, is unremarkable for a core network node or a substantial data-hall build. Even a confirmed figure would be consistent with the commercial null.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Grokipedia pages on 'Project Offices' and on the Hadley PACCS facility constitute additional sources.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: Grokipedia, a machine-generated encyclopedia, mirroring the corresponding Wikipedia articles.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Under §3.3 these are POST-2022-UNATTRIBUTED and sit on the versioned blocklist of machine-generated corpora: T5, zero contribution to every condition, zero lineages, retained and displayed. I record them because they surfaced repeatedly in this session's search results ALONGSIDE the Wikipedia articles they mirror, which creates exactly the false appearance of breadth the rule exists to prevent. An automated ingest counting distinct domains would score this as two sources. It is one, and the one is already T4.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: A machine-generated encyclopedia restated an existing encyclopedia article. Nothing was learned and nothing was added.

refuted_or_hollow.claim: Netcong, New Jersey was one of the AT&T Project Offices.
refuted_or_hollow.origin: A conflation in this session's own search results, where a query naming several candidate sites returned the Netcong CLUI entry among Project Office material and the summary presented them as members of one set.
refuted_or_hollow.why_hollow: Recorded as a finding against my own process rather than against a source. The Project Office chain, per both coldwar-c4i.net and CLUI, is five mid-Atlantic TROPOSCATTER stations running Hagerstown–Short Hill–Peters Mountain–Buckingham–Chatham. Netcong is a different object: AT&T's underground network operations centre in northern New Jersey, with no troposcatter role reported. I have excluded it from the chain entry and given it its own. The near-miss is worth publishing because a candidate-set rule (§9.2 C1c) is only as good as the set's boundary, and an erroneously admitted sixth member would have inflated M and diluted every genuine member's grade.
refuted_or_hollow.mundane_explanation: Two AT&T underground buildings of the same era in adjacent regions, described in similar language by the same compilations, retrieved by one query.

coverage_gaps:
WHAT THIS SWEEP DID NOT TOUCH, in rough order of how much it matters.

1. EVERY CANONICAL CORPUS. No FCC ASR or ULS, no county recorder or assessor in any of the eleven counties named above, no USGS HTMC temporal stack, no GovInfo, no NARA, no CREST, no DTIC, no AFHRA, no FRPP, no GSA disposal. This is not a prioritisation choice; the hosts are unreachable. It means the beat's central promise — that FCC registrations and infrastructure records give it real documentary anchors — is entirely unredeemed by this cycle. The anchors were identified; none was pulled.

2. THE WESTERN UNION SIDE OF THE HOUSE. The literature is overwhelmingly AT&T-shaped. Western Union ran a parallel hardened government microwave network including the Washington Area Wideband System, with named nodes at the Naval Security Station, NSA's Friendship Annex, Andrews AFB, Liberty Dam and the Alternate Joint Communications Center. I found the system's name, an acronym that will index well in federal corpora, a route map, and a peer-reviewed scholarly treatment of the company's microwave programme (Rotenstein 2006) — and I searched none of the federal corpora for 'WAWS'. This is the largest unexplored seam I found and I would rank it first for the next cycle.

3. AUTOVON AS A SYSTEM. Reports of 'at least 38' hardened switching centres circulate; I developed one (Pottstown PA) barely and named Cheshire CT and Monrovia MD without developing them at all. AUTOVON has a published architecture, a documented DCA lineage and a finite switch list, which makes it a far more tractable candidate-set target than 'Project Offices'. A full enumeration of the AUTOVON switch list against county records would be a productive dedicated cycle.

4. THE L-CARRIER BURIED PLANT. Roughly a thousand hardened repeater vaults were built along the L-3I and L-4 routes — concrete vaults under small surface huts at roughly four-mile spacing along continuous cross-country rights of way. These are the most numerous hardened structures in the United States and are almost entirely unregistered anywhere. They are also, individually, near-worthless as candidates and collectively very valuable as a mapped route. The right treatment is a route geometry with a PROGRAM proposition, not a thousand entries, and I did not attempt it.

5. FEDERAL SPECTRUM. As the source registry states, the networks that actually served continuity-of-government facilities were licensed through NTIA/IRAC and are absent from the FCC record by construction. Everything findable on this beat is the commercial shadow of an invisible federal system. The register should state this on every comms entry rather than treating FCC silence as meaningful.

6. THE FUNDING QUESTION. Whether the AT&T Project Offices were built with AT&T capital, with federal money, or on a cost-shared basis is the single fact that would most reorganise this beat — it determines whether MILCON, DD-1391 and FPDS profiles are X0 or X3, and therefore whether the documentary silence around these five stations is uninformative or damning. I could not establish it and I do not think anyone in the open literature has.

7. ORIGIN WORK PROPER. No Wayback CDX sweep, no IA full-text hits_inside, no Chronicling America or Open ONI search of construction-era local press in Chatham, Buckingham, Washington, Albemarle, Loudoun, Burt, Boone, Morris or Hampshire counties. Every claim-origin trace in this file is therefore an EARLIEST APPEARANCE I HAPPENED TO FIND, not a receipted earliest appearance, and no ORIGIN proposition is offered anywhere in this file for that reason. Note specifically that the 1960s construction-era local press for most of these sites falls after 1963, which is where Chronicling America's free corpus stops for copyright reasons — a real, specific, structural archive gap that will need a paid database.

8. AT&T'S OWN CORPORATE RECORD. Bell System Practices, Bell Laboratories Record articles, Long Lines route and plant engineering literature, and the AT&T Archives. Per the calibration set, this is the class of document that carries D3 for hardening claims on this typology, and it is the class that would collapse a dozen compiler-dependent propositions into properly sourced ones at a stroke. The archives.long-lines.com mirror of L4 documentation and the qsl.net transcription are both pointers into it and neither was followed.

9. GEOLOCATION. Zero coordinates resolved, deliberately (see method_notes). Every candidate needs a parcel or ASR pull before it can carry a LOCATE proposition at any band, and several are trivially obtainable — the Lyons site has a published street address and a registered 329-foot tower; the Missouri repeaters have ASR numbers with surveyed coordinates.
